items.text: Survey: one log clear (rec 887106) followed 9 s later by eleven Kerberos events from 172.16.66.1 within about 23 ms, and recognised the host as a domain controller because it logs 4768/4771
Decoded the results: 0x6 with NULL SID = account doesn't exist (7 names), 0x18 = account exists but wrong password (Administrator, backdoor), 0x0 = TGT issued (normal)
Identified the pattern as password spraying (one attempt per account, many accounts, one source, machine speed) that also revealed which accounts exist
Concluded the account 'normal' is compromised (rec 887116), and noticed the second TGT (rec 887117) uses the ::ffff: address form and a different source port range
Read the log clear correctly: by 3B\a-jbrown, logon 0x3a17a, before the spray, so it couldn't have hidden it; noted 1102 has no source IP
Kept the log clear and the spray as separate findings unless linked by evidence, and named what would link them (e.g. the 4624 for logon 0x3a17a)
Flagged the existing account named 'backdoor' (rec 887115) for review without claiming when or by whom it was created
Noted TicketOptions 0x10 as unlike a normal Windows client, presented as supporting context rather than proof
Listed at least three things the logs can't tell you (e.g. who is at 172.16.66.1, what normal did next, why the log was cleared)

Classified it as a true positive and recommended resetting normal, finding the source machine, checking normal's later 4769/4624 activity, verifying the log clear with the admin, and reviewing 'backdoor'
